executive_summary: OFAC added 12 new entities to the SDN list, primarily targeting individuals and entities involved in SDGT and IFSR programs, with a focus on Iran, China, and the United Arab Emirates. The additions highlight the ongoing efforts to disrupt and sanction malicious activities. The majority of the added entities are linked to the IRGC program, indicating a continued focus on countering Iranian malign activities.

notable_entities.name: Zadeh Ahmad Mohammadi
notable_entities.significance: High-ranking individual in the IRGC, added to the SDN list for involvement in SDGT and IFSR programs

notable_entities.name: Salami Samad Fathi
notable_entities.significance: Individual involved in SDGT and IFSR programs, linked to the IRGC

notable_entities.name: Ghehi Mohammadreza Ashrafi
notable_entities.significance: Individual involved in SDGT and IFSR programs, linked to the IRGC

risk_implications.description: The addition of 12 new entities to the SDN list, primarily targeting Iranian and Chinese individuals and entities, may indicate an increased risk of sanctions evasion and terrorist financing in the region
The sanctions may impact global trade, particularly in the shipping and logistics sectors, as several entities added to the list are involved in these industries

program_highlights.note: All 12 added entities are involved in the SDGT program, highlighting the ongoing efforts to disrupt and sanction terrorist organizations
All 12 added entities are also involved in the IFSR program, indicating a focus on countering Iranian malign activities
Three individuals added to the list are linked to the IRGC, highlighting the continued focus on countering Iranian military activities

compliance_recommendations: Conduct thorough due diligence on all business partners and clients, particularly those involved in high-risk industries such as shipping and logistics
Implement effective sanctions screening and monitoring programs to detect and prevent transactions with sanctioned entities
Stay up-to-date with the latest sanctions developments and adjust compliance programs accordingly
